data.description:
How to make your own AI film crew.

With invideo Agent Two you can create roles for each virtual crew member, and it will spin up individual agents that can work alongside you and your existing crew.

Filmmaking is evolving. Instead of just prompting, work alongside AI that understands what you want, supporting your vision so you can spend less time on the technical, and more time on the creative.

We partnered with invideo to create our sci-fi survival horror short film No Up, No Down using Agent Two.

In this video we break down our process, and how we created the short film from beginning to end.

#aifilmmaking #invideoagenttwo #aifilm #ai #makingof
data.transcript: In this video, we're going to show you how to make your own AI film crew just like we did for our latest viral film No Up, No Down, all using the best AI agent for creative work, InVideo Agent 2. Let's go. Normally when you're creating a film there's the same general workflow: come up with the concept, write the script, develop the look, make the characters, generate the keyframe images, generate the videos and then edit. With InVideo Agent 2 that workflow is completely flipped on its head. Agent 2 works like an entire film crew. You create each role and InVideo will spin up an agent for that specific thing. This can be assistant director, concept artist, cinematographer, whatever you need. It's almost like making a movie in a video game. You can even play multiplayer with your real life team working alongside the AI agents serving as your digital crew, all without ever needing to re-explain anything that's already been covered, because Agent 2 is incredibly smart and remembers everything you tell it. We're going to start by creating a new role and naming it Creative Producer. This will ensure we stay in the director's seat. Then we tell it what we want it to do: Act as my creative producer. Don't invent the movie for me, just ask questions about the concept for more clarity, identify missing decisions that need to be made, create shot lists, suggest coverage and flag weak story logic. Keep every choice consistent with the director's vision. Then give it context about your project so it can fully understand what you're trying to make, and InVideo Agent 2 can remember context across your entire film! No Up No Down is a sci-fi action survival horror set in space that follows two soldiers sent to intervene at an enemy space station that has become overrun with genetically engineered creatures which are now on the loose from the ship wreaking havoc. Once you have the idea nailed down it's time to start designing the look of the film. First off we're going to create our characters and props. Make a new role and name it concept artist, then we can start generating. You can switch between Lite, Pro and Ultra based on how much intelligence you need for a given task. From here again speak to your AI concept artist in plain language, get their help with designing your characters: Help me create a tactical soldier in a realistic sci-fi space suit. InVideo Agent 2 has access to all the latest models like Nano Banana Pro and Seedance 2.5. The image models are perfect for creating character reference sheets. Just start with an image of your character and ask for a character reference turnaround. This is going to show your characters from every angle so they can stay consistent throughout your film. Once it's created you can tweak it as much until you get exactly the design that you're looking for, then do the same process with all props. When I have my film's items like weapons, vehicles like spaceships, one to three images of all the characters and props, it's time to start generating the videos. This is the most crucial part of this workflow! First let's make a new role and name it Director Of Photography, then type in your brief: Act as my director of photography, create each shot based on the director's vision and project brief. We're going to also add a playbook for this agent. You can think about a playbook as a set of rules that your digital crew member will follow for their specific role. For Project No Up No Down: all image generations Nano Banana Pro 4K 16x9, all video generation Seedance 2.0 1080p 16x9, no other models or settings unless Lion says otherwise. Then you can add more details that are specific to your film: I'm creating a dark filmic sci-fi action survival horror. It needs to be incredibly cinematic with very filmic qualities. Keep going from here, the more clear you are the better. Often times Agent 2 will then ask you a quick series of questions to get even more clarity. This is gonna save you a ton of time during the generation process by getting what you want nailed down in advance. From here, you can just ask for what you want in plain language just like you're talking to someone on set. You can ask things like: Can we do a 15 second shot of the drop ship speeding towards the space station with a realistic handheld camera, do 4 generations. Or animate this title design, create four 5 second generations. You're just asking for what you want and InVideo Agent 2 will just do it, allowing you to make changes and experiment along the way. If you ask for something that requires multiple departments, like design a new title card image and then animate it, the concept artist can start it and then another department like your director of photography can pick it up to generate the videos. As you go just download the clips you want and you can start to edit. I tend to edit as I go, especially with AI filmmaking. By editing as you go you see what's working and exactly which shots need regenerating to make everything work. Many filmmakers first starting off with AI filmmaking are often surprised at how much more creative you can get at this stage, as opposed to exclusively filming on set. Often times in traditional films there's not enough time or money to coordinate serious reshoots, but with AI filmmaking you can reshoot as you go. InVideo makes this easy because it is insanely fast. You can try things out, see what works and pivot into entirely new directions. Beyond that, Agent 2 remembers every conversation and keeps that context across your entire project. The agents even communicate with each other just like a crew on a digital film set! This is the Claude Code moment for filmmaking, the same way engineers felt when they could simply describe their intent and the agents would take over to execute on their vision, it's now coming into film. Once you have everything edited all that's left to do is export it. If you want to see the full film, you can check out No Up No Down on our page or at the end of this video. InVideo Agent 2 is an unbelievably fast agent designed specifically for filmmakers, so try it out for yourself at invideo.io with the link in the description and we'll see you in the next one.

Comment ‘invideo’ and we’ll send you the exact timeline we used.

If you’re using match cuts in your video, the invideo editor + agent gives you the fastest, most seamless experience to do it. Generate your footage with a constant subject, place your audio track and ask the agent to mark out the beats, have the agent place your footage on those beats, and you’re done. Works on any subject, and any style.

Comment MATCH and I’ll send you the exact prompt I used. 👇

This is probably one of the easiest ways I’ve found to create a generative match cut like this.

Start by recording a simple clip of yourself throwing an object into the air.

Then head over to InVideo and open their new Timeline Editor, which is completely free to use. Add an AI agent directly to your timeline and upload your raw footage.

Now paste in the prompt and simply describe what you want to change during the match cut. In my case, I wanted my T-shirt to transform.

Hit enter and the agent starts building the entire effect directly on your timeline. You can literally watch the edit come together.

And the best part? If something isn’t exactly how you want it, just tell the agent what to change and it adjusts the edit for you.

A generative match cut without having to build everything manually. 🤯🎬

@invideo.io
